pr.title: Wait for a pull request to be ready before reviewing it
pr.head: 7fa6904c67e437ac1d38a85ed0d2e446a8e32022

summary: Projector's watch daemon is one process per machine. It polls the pull requests that agent sessions subscribe to, and tells each session what to do with a one-line event, such as NEW HEAD when a pull request has a head that no review has read. A repository subscription, which the review-repo skill adds, covers every pull request in a repository. A pull request subscription, which review-pr adds, covers one pull request.

The layer below this one moved Projector's sign-off from draft state to a clean label and a projector/review commit status. A draft can now mean what GitHub means by it: the author is still working. This layer makes the daemon act on that, so a pull request whose design is still moving costs no reviews until its author marks it ready.

• Repository subscriptions wait for ready. For a draft, the daemon announces no NEW PR, NEW HEAD, reminder, or RESPONDED. It keeps the pull request's record, and when the author marks it ready, it announces whatever no review read.
  • Pull request subscriptions still announce drafts. A person who runs review-pr on a draft asks for its review now, so every head and RESPONDED still arrive.
  • UNREVIEWED replaces DRAFT. The session that fixes a pull request hears it, once per head, for a ready pull request whose head is not signed off and that no session on this machine reviews.
  • One sign-off rule. The daemon now decides sign-off with review.sign_off, the function project review publish uses, in place of its own copy.

cards.title: Projector review of 7fa6904
cards.html:
The newest review is clean. The one earlier finding is settled as fixed. It was that a review that stalled while its pull request was a draft lost the notice that tells the session to stop the stalled subagent. 7fa6904 now reports that notice on the draft, and the earlier reproduction passes.

The full unit suite, project check, and git diff --check passed on this head. One suggestion stands: say in the stalled NEW HEAD bullet of review-pr, and in the events table, that the draft variant asks the session to wait for ready.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Record: what the daemon stores per session and pull request: the last head it knew (head), when it last announced one (announced), and the answer it last saw (flag).
  • Reminder: the NEW HEAD … (still open) line the daemon repeats every watch.renotify seconds while a head waits on a review.
  • Signed off: the newest counted Projector verdict on the head is clean, and no Projector finding thread is open.
  • Stalled review: a review whose lock no project review command touched for watch.review_stall seconds.

groups.title: The daemon waits on a draft's author
groups.kicker: Event routing in the watch daemon, and the sign-off rule it shares with publish
intro: Two functions in watch.py decide what each session hears. route_review serves a session that reviews a pull request, and route_fix serves one that fixes it.

In route_review, a draft under a repository subscription now returns before any line is built. The record it saves sets up the ready transition. The last head it knew stays, so a head pushed while the pull request was a draft becomes a NEW HEAD. A head that was announced and never reviewed gets announced set to 0, so the reminder fires at once on ready rather than after watch.renotify. One exception remains: a review that stalls while the pull request is a draft is reported once. The report is a NEW HEAD line that tells the session to stop the stalled subagent and to review the pull request once it is ready.
In route_fix, UNREVIEWED replaces DRAFT. It fires only for a ready pull request whose head is not signed off. A live start comment from an account whose review would count still holds it back.

Both functions now call head_sign_off, which hands the review nodes from the daemon's GraphQL query to review.sign_off. The reviewer's own verdicts count whatever association GitHub gives the account, as they already did for publish.

files.note: The draft gate in route_review, UNREVIEWED in route_fix, and verdict_rows with head_sign_off in place of head_verdicts.

checks.text: The stall line on a draft. I reran the earlier reproduction on this head: the pass that clears a stalled lock sends this line. Marking the pull request ready then sends the (still open) reminder at once, because announced is set to 0.

UNREVIEWED needs three things: the pull request is not a draft, no session on this machine owns its review, and its head is not signed off. The live-start-comment check below it only holds the event back.

The rows verdict_rows builds carry no id or url. Traced through newest_verdicts and with_full_review: ordering falls back to the submit time, and an incremental review's link to its full review never matches, which affects only the suggestion count the daemon does not read here.

files.note: New ReviewRoleTests cases for the draft gate and the ready transition, and FixRoleTests rewritten for UNREVIEWED.

checks.text: FixRoleTests now makes every pull request a draft unless a test says otherwise, so only the tests about review coverage hear UNREVIEWED.
This test fails if the draft gate ignores the subscription's kind: it expects a pull request subscription to announce a draft's first head.
This test covers a stall on a draft: one stop notice, nothing on the next pass, and the reminder once the pull request is ready.

groups.title: Skills and documentation describe the wait
groups.kicker: The events table, three skills, and two plans
intro: The skills tell agents what each event means, so they change with the daemon. review-repo says drafts wait for ready and that running review-pr on a draft asks for its review now. review-pr says its own subscription announces drafts. fix-pr describes UNREVIEWED in place of DRAFT.

docs/cli.md carries the events table and a new paragraph on drafts. The review-on-ready plan records the decisions this layer settled in § 9.2, and the in-progress watch-daemon plan updates its events table.
